reasons.plausibility: The hypothesis is physically sound, linking thermal expansion mismatch and residual stresses to mechanical behavior, but it overstates the role of residual stresses in governing high-temperature creep and elastic moduli, where dislocation climb and intrinsic bonding typically dominate.
reasons.testability: The proposed test is clear and feasible, but the falsification criterion is weak because residual stresses will inevitably relax at 1250 °C before creep testing, making the predicted difference in creep rates unlikely to manifest.
reasons.usefulness: The hypothesis usefully integrates several disparate observations into a single framework, but its practical value is limited by the difficulty of isolating residual stress effects from concurrent microstructural changes (dislocations, precipitates) and the questionable persistence of stresses at high temperatures.
